_meta.note: Structural regression golden. 7 annotations stripped (— one sentence ×5, — 2-4 sentences ×2) that were glued onto primary copy-paste output (opener message/subject_line/follow_up.message/power_move/label) — check:golden checks STRUCTURE not content, eyeball wording after prompt edits. Already on callClaudeWithRetry (no robustness gap). Guard: !openers && !situation_read (top-level). Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v2): power_move and response_rate removed. The power move proposed publishing a public rebuttal and tagging the recipient before contacting them — an escalation nobody asked for. response_rate predicted a stranger's behaviour nobody measured. boldness (safe/medium/bold) stays: it describes the message rather than the reply. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v3): the output was explaining itself more than helping. boldness (safe/medium/bold), why_it_works and best_if are gone from each opener — a risk badge is a measurement of a message nobody has seen received, and the commentary ran longer than the deliverable. what_not_to_say (3-5 cautions) collapsed to a single optional before_you_send line, because most of that list was the model reporting its own epistemic hygiene back to the visitor. follow_up_plan {when,message,when_to_stop} became follow_up {message,timing}: the stopping rule and the closing-window language asserted things about the recipient's calendar that nothing established. situation_read is now nullable and usually null. subject_line must contain the subject and nothing else — it was coming back as "Included inside each message above.", which renders to the visitor AS their subject line, with the real subject duplicated inside all three bodies. Prompt also carries a reaction-vs-role rule: "I shipped X, so your post landed" is the sender's own reaction and is fine; "reliability at that scale is where most of my time goes" is a job claim nobody supplied. Adopted PF-39 v2 at this lock. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v4): added enforceSuppliedFacts — an adversarial second pass that checks every first-person claim in the drafts against the four form fields, then repairs only the offending messages. The prompt alone had failed three reviews running: a job role invented from a shipped project, then an opinion ("the most concrete thing I have read"), an action ("I sent it to my team the day it went up") and a motive ("made Stripe feel like the right fit"). The form fields ARE the envelope here, so no assembly is needed. Fail-open, verdict logged on every call. Also: an opinion SWAPPED for the supplied one counts as invention ("thoughtful" is not "stuck with me"), and follow_up.timing may no longer say what people commonly do.

input.who: the VP of Engineering at a mid-size fintech startup I admire
input.why: I want to explore a senior backend role on her team
input.whatYouKnow: She wrote a widely-shared blog post about scaling payments infrastructure and mentors women in tech
input.yourBackground: 8 years backend, led a payments migration

openers.label: Names the ask straight away, anchors on shared domain
openers.message:
Hi [Name],

I came across your post on scaling payments infrastructure and thought it was worth reaching out directly. I have eight years of backend experience and recently led a payments migration, so the subject is close to home.

I am interested in senior backend roles and would love to know if there is anything open on your team. Happy to share more about my background if useful.

openers.label: Leads with the blog post, then makes the ask
openers.message:
Hi [Name],

I read your post on scaling payments infrastructure and thought it was thoughtful. It prompted me to look into the team more closely.

I have spent eight years in backend engineering and recently led a payments migration. If you have senior backend openings, I would be glad to be considered — or if you could point me toward the right person, that would be helpful too.

openers.label: Opens with background, asks for a short conversation
openers.message:
Hi [Name],

I am a backend engineer with eight years of experience, including leading a payments migration. I read your post on scaling payments infrastructure and am interested in exploring whether there might be a senior backend role that fits.

Would you be open to a brief conversation? No pressure if the timing is off.

output.before_you_send: Confirm her name is spelled correctly before sending.

follow_up.message:
Hi [Name],

Just following up on my previous message in case it got buried. Happy to share more about my background whenever it suits you.
follow_up.timing: Give the first message some room before sending this; adjust if you have a specific deadline in mind.
